answer: For a standard reimbursement claim, you have 30 days from the date of discharge to submit [2]. However, for Aurora Group Health corporate plans, the submission window is 60 days from discharge [3], while an archived 2024 timeline lists the deadline as 15 days from discharge [1].
The room rent limit on the Aurora Silver plan is 2% of the sum insured per day [3].
No, maternity cover is not available on the Bronze plan at any sum insured [1][2].

The waiting period for pre-existing diseases is 36 months on retail plans, under the Aurora Hospital Cash Benefit, and for conditions such as hypertension, diabetes, and cardiac conditions unless explicitly waived [2][4][5]. However, under the Aurora Senior Care plan for ages 60 and above, the waiting period is 24 months [2].
The grace period for an annual policy is 30 days [1][2].
As of 1 April 2026, Aurora's network covers 11,400 hospitals across 780 towns [1].

Under the Aurora Gold plan, the no-claim bonus is 25% of the base sum insured for each claim-free year, accumulating up to a maximum of 100% [1][4]. The accumulated bonus is not reduced if a claim is made; it only stops accumulating for that year [1].
No, you cannot claim for IVF treatment [1]. Infertility, assisted reproduction, IVF, surrogacy, and sterilisation reversal are listed as permanent treatment-related exclusions [1].
Under the Aurora Gold plan, the sub-limit for cataract surgery is ₹75,000 per eye [1].

If you are not satisfied with the initial Stage 1 outcome, you can escalate to Aurora's Grievance Redressal Officer [1]. If Aurora's final response is unsatisfactory, you can approach the Insurance Ombudsman for your region, provided the dispute meets certain criteria such as a claim value under ₹50,00,000 [3]. You also retain the right to escalate the matter to a consumer forum or civil court [3].

There is an ambulance cover of ₹5,000 per hospitalisation for road ambulance only, which is common to all plans [1]. This ₹5,000 limit per hospitalisation is also specified in both the Silver and Bronze plan terms [3][5].
Yes, in-patient treatment for mental illness is covered on the same terms as physical illness [1]. The standard 30-day initial waiting period applies, with no separate waiting period required [1].

The free-look period is the window in which a new policy can be returned for a refund [5]. It lasts 15 days from receiving the policy document, or 30 days if the policy was sold through distance marketing [1][2]. A policyholder who cancels during this time receives a refund of the premium less the proportionate risk premium for the period of cover, medical examination costs, and stamp duty [2].
You earn 150 wellness points for completing an annual health check-up [1].

A day-care procedure is a procedure that requires less than 24 hours of hospitalisation because of technological advances, making it payable despite the general 24-hour admission requirement [2]. Out-patient treatment is not considered a day-care procedure [2].
For a cashless emergency admission, the hospital must notify Aurora within 24 hours of admission [1].
No, Aurora administers its own claims and does not use a Third Party Administrator (TPA) [1].
To qualify as a hospital under the policy, a facility must have at least 10 in-patient beds in towns with a population below 10 lakh, or at least 15 in-patient beds elsewhere [1].

No, everything will not be fully paid [1][2]. Under the Silver plan with a ₹5,00,000 sum insured, the room-rent limit is 2% (₹10,000 per day), so occupying a room at ₹15,000 per day triggers a proportionate deduction [1][2]. While pharmacy and consumables are not reduced, the room rent and all associated medical charges tied to the room category will be proportionately reduced, leaving out-of-pocket expenses [1][2].

Dependent parents can be added under the Silver plan (for an extra premium), as well as the Gold and Platinum plans, but not the Bronze plan [2]. Adding her will cause the policy's premium to be calculated based on her age if she is the eldest member [3]. Additionally, on the Silver plan, having an eldest member over 60 introduces a 10% co-payment on every claim [4].

Waiting periods already served with your previous insurer will carry over, but only up to the sum insured of your previous policy, including any accrued no-claim bonus [1][2]. Any increase in the sum insured will be subject to fresh waiting periods on the incremental amount [1][2].

To continue insurance cover for your newborn beyond the first 90 days, you must inform Aurora and add the baby to your policy as a dependent within 90 days of birth [1]. If requested within this 90-day window, adding the newborn is guaranteed-issue without medical underwriting; after this window, the child is treated as a fresh applicant [1].

A claim reduces your accumulated no-claim bonus by 10 percentage points, rather than resetting it to zero [1].
Under the Gold plan, the maternity limit for a Caesarean section is ₹1,00,000 per delivery [1]. If the hospital bills ₹1,60,000, you would pay ₹60,000 out of pocket [1].

Knee joint replacement is generally not covered immediately, as it is subject to a 24-month waiting period [2][3]. However, if the knee replacement is required following an accidental injury, it is covered from day one with no waiting period [2][3].

Discounts are generally capped at 30% of the base premium [1]. However, an additional wellness discount of up to 15% at renewal is applied after the cap and is the only discount permitted to exceed it [1][4].

Cashless access is not available at an excluded provider [1][2]. Your only option is to seek reimbursement with pre-approval, which is payable only if the admission was a genuine emergency and no alternative facility was reachable [2].
For health reimbursement claims, you have 45 days from the date of the query to respond [1]. For motor insurance claims, you have 30 days from the date of the query to respond [4].

For a planned cashless admission, notification must be submitted at least 72 hours before admission [2][3]. However, the sources show a disagreement, as an archived policy document lists the deadline as 48 hours before admission [1].

Aurora settles or rejects a complete reimbursement claim within 15 working days of receiving the last required document [1][2]. If Aurora raises a query, the timeline restarts once the queried document is supplied [1]. (Under archived 2024 rules, the reimbursement settlement timeline was 30 days [3]).
Aurora Gold has no co-payment at all ages [1]. Additionally, Aurora Silver has no co-payment when the eldest insured member is below age 60 [2].

The pre- and post-hospitalisation coverage windows for each plan are as follows:
- **Bronze:** 30 days pre-hospitalisation and 60 days post-hospitalisation [1].
- **Silver:** 45 days pre-hospitalisation and 90 days post-hospitalisation [1].
- **Gold:** 60 days pre-hospitalisation and 120 days post-hospitalisation [1].
- **Platinum:** 90 days pre-hospitalisation and 180 days post-hospitalisation [1].
You should choose the Gold plan (or Platinum) [2][5]. The Gold plan removes room-rent and ICU sub-limits, and both the Gold and Platinum plans cover dependent parents-in-law [2][5].

Dental treatment and oral surgery are permanently excluded, unless necessitated by an accidental injury requiring hospitalisation [2]. Additionally, out-patient dental work is not covered by any plan [1].

For health insurance, you lose accumulated no-claim bonuses and waiting-period continuity if you do not pay within the grace period, which is 30 days for annual policies and 15 days for instalment policies [1]. For Aurora Life insurance, a policy lapses after a grace period of 30 days (annual, half-yearly, quarterly) or 15 days (monthly), at which point term policies provide no cover, while endowment policies with surrender value continue at a reduced sum assured [2][4].

Denial of cashless access is not a rejection of your claim [1]. If cashless was denied because the supplied information was insufficient to establish medical necessity or the condition appeared to fall within an unexpired waiting period, you can pay the hospital and file for reimbursement [1]. A material proportion of denied cashless requests are subsequently settled through the reimbursement route when assessed against the full document set [1].
Completing the quit-tobacco programme earns 200 wellness points per year [1]. These points convert toward a renewal-premium discount at a rate of 5% per 1,000 points, capped at 15% [1][5].
